ROW.COLUMN: (FR/AC) High Risk Transactions: High Risk Geography

Increasingly, fraud is being perpetrated by organized crime rings who leverage increasingly sophisticated fraud techniques and advanced technology methods to gain access to significant numbers of customer accounts. Many of these rings are based overseas. The subsequent movement of funds, both within and outside of the institution, can become quite complicated as the fraudsters attempt to hide their tracks and make potential recovery impossible by moving defrauded funds offshore. Because of the large volume and speed of transactions, electronic funds transactions are considered particularly vulnerable to money laundering. This scenario identifies accounts or entities that may be at risk for fraud based on the incidence of electronic funds transfers, checks, or monetary instrument transactions involving specified high-risk geographic areas.
